concepts.name: Internal Audit
concepts.description: An audit conducted by an organization on itself to verify compliance with its own QMS requirements

concepts.name: Supplier Audit
concepts.description: An audit conducted by an organization on its suppliers to verify their capability and compliance

concepts.name: Certification Audit
concepts.description: An audit conducted by a certification body to determine if an organization meets requirements for certification

concepts.name: FMEA
concepts.description: Failure Mode and Effects Analysis - A systematic method for identifying potential failure modes and their effects

concepts.name: APQP
concepts.description: Advanced Product Quality Planning - A structured approach to product development and launch

concepts.name: PPAP
concepts.description: Production Part Approval Process - A standardized process for approving production parts

concepts.name: SPC
concepts.description: Statistical Process Control - Use of statistical methods to monitor and control processes

concepts.name: MSA
concepts.description: Measurement System Analysis - Evaluation of measurement systems to ensure accuracy and precision

concepts.name: Control Plan
concepts.description: A document that describes the methods for controlling production processes

concepts.name: 8D
concepts.description: Eight Disciplines problem-solving methodology for root cause analysis and corrective action

concepts.name: Ishikawa Diagram
concepts.description: Fishbone diagram used for root cause analysis, showing potential causes of a problem

concepts.name: 5 Whys
concepts.description: A simple root cause analysis technique that asks 'why' five times to get to the root cause

concepts.name: DOE
concepts.description: Design of Experiments - A systematic method for determining relationships between factors and outcomes

concepts.name: Procedure
concepts.description: A document that describes how to perform a process or activity

concepts.name: Work Instruction
concepts.description: A detailed document that describes how to perform a specific task

concepts.name: Form
concepts.description: A structured document used to collect and record information

concepts.name: Record
concepts.description: Evidence of activities performed or results achieved

concepts.name: Quality Manual
concepts.description: A document that describes the organization's quality management system

concepts.name: QMS Matrix
concepts.description: A matrix showing how the organization's processes map to standard requirements

concepts.name: Lead Auditor
concepts.description: The auditor responsible for planning, conducting, and reporting on an audit

concepts.name: Internal Auditor
concepts.description: An auditor who conducts internal audits within their own organization

concepts.name: Quality Manager
concepts.description: The person responsible for managing the quality management system

concepts.name: Process Owner
concepts.description: The person responsible for a specific process within the QMS

concepts.name: Inspector
concepts.description: A person who performs inspection activities to verify product or process conformity

concepts.name: NCR
concepts.description: Nonconformity Report - A document that records a nonconformity found during an audit or inspection

concepts.name: CAR
concepts.description: Corrective Action Request - A formal request to address a nonconformity and prevent recurrence

concepts.name: SCAR
concepts.description: Supplier Corrective Action Request - A CAR issued to a supplier

concepts.name: Risk Assessment
concepts.description: The process of identifying, analyzing, and evaluating risks

concepts.name: Management Review
concepts.description: A periodic review by top management of the QMS to ensure its continuing suitability and effectiveness

concepts.name: Calibration
concepts.description: The process of verifying and adjusting measuring equipment to ensure accuracy

concepts.name: Training
concepts.description: The process of providing education and training to personnel to ensure competence

concepts.name: Design Control
concepts.description: The process of controlling design and development activities to ensure requirements are met

metadata.description: APQP is the planning phase that leads to PPAP approval
FMEA identifies risks that flow into Control Plans
A nonconformity typically triggers a corrective action request
Procedures are implemented through work instructions
8D methodology may use Ishikawa diagrams for root cause analysis
5 Whys and Ishikawa diagrams are complementary root cause analysis tools
